text:
Sam: Quick update — I pushed an initial 'az15-edge' init playbook to infra/runbooks and did a smoke dry-run provisioning (small pool) this morning. Found a couple of hard blockers + a few operational gotchas. Repo: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/runbooks/az15-init

Jordan: link? saw CI flagged something earlier.

Sam: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/runbooks/az15-init (README + checklist). Dry-run notes pasted below.

Sam: Terraform apply failed on one step with a public IP quota error. Command and error:
```bash
$ terraform apply -var region=az15-edge -auto-approve
Error: create_public_ip: InsufficientPublicIPs: ExceededPublicIPQuota
status code: 429
message: You have reached the maximum number of public IPs for subscription xxxxx
```

Priya: Ugh. We hit that in az9 before — quick wins: 1) request quota bump, 2) use NAT Gateway + private nodes to avoid per-node public IPs, 3) recycle unused ephemeral IPs. Which did the dry-run use?

Sam: Dry-run used per-node public IPs because we were validating remote-access/serial logs without bastion in the first pass.

Maya: For cost: NAT gateway is cheaper long-term vs many static public IPs. But initial setup adds a couple hundred USD/month. If quota bump timeline is fast (AWS/Azure request in ~24-48h) we could patch the playbook to use a temporary NAT and then flip to private nodes later.

Li: Also saw intermittent control-plane flaps during kubelet join — network logs show BGP hold timer expiry toward our edge router. Snippet: 
```text
Mar 08 08:12:04 node-3 bgp[2345]: %ROUTE-5-HOLDTIMER: hold timer expired, dropping session with 10.8.0.1
Mar 08 08:12:05 node-3 kernel: netlink: route attribute overflow
```

Jordan: That smells like MTU mismatch or a mis-applied rewrite on the transit vxlan. Did we apply the VXLAN MTU 1450 on the hypervisor template?

Li: I checked — hypervisor template used MTU 1500. Need explicit 1450 for ifencap overhead. Running a test now to repro with ping + DF bit.

Sam: Good catch. I'll add an MTU verification step to the runbook (preflight). Proposed snippet:
```bash
# preflight MTU check
ip link add testvx type vxlan id 42 dev eth0 dstport 4789 || true
ip link set dev testvx mtu 1450 || true
ping -M do -s 1400 <peer> -c 3
```

Priya: Also add a check for cloud-provider route propagation — earlier we had a case where cloud NAT removed route advertisements and nodes lost default route for a few minutes. Add: validate that all subnets have a route to the transit and a fallback to the private egress.

Sam: Noted, adding to checklist.

Jordan: Minor: during the dry-run we saw GPU SKU mismatch on the GPU pool request — request asked for "a100-40gb" but the AZ advertised only "a100-80gb" and a spot SKU. Terraform happily created spot instances and they joined but our scheduler refused non-standard labels. Error: node-gpu: label mismatch: "gpu.memory": "80Gi" != "40Gi"

Sam: I forced a rollback to a temporary config that maps a100-80 -> a100-compatible, but we need a proper mapping table in the runbook and a policy for fallback SKUs.

Maya: For handoff to Capacity team: include a SKU compatibility matrix and cost delta table (spot vs on-demand, 40GB vs 80GB). Ops should pre-approve fallback to spot for non-prod only.

Priya: Also, add a step validating node-labeling + taint application order. We had a race where kubelet applied labels after scheduling decisions, causing pods to land wrong. Sequence to document: create node -> set taints -> wait for kubelet-ready -> apply labels -> then allow schedule.

Sam: Adding that ordering as a required step & automated check (kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath...).

Sam: I'm pasting a short template for the handoff checklist — plz review:
```text
Handoff checklist for az15-edge provisioning:
- Confirm region quota (compute, publicIPs, GPUS) [owner: Capacity]
- KMS key & CMK replication configured [owner: Security]
- VPC/Peering established + route leak test (BGP hold timers) [owner: NetEng]
- MTU validation across hypervisors and VXLAN [owner: NetEng]
- GPU SKU matrix + fallback policy [owner: Capacity]
- Prometheus/alerting scrape targets + cost tags [owner: Observability]
- NAT gateway plan for reducing public IP usage (temp vs final) [owner: Infra]
- Runbook dry-run artifacts uploaded (logs + terraform state) [owner: Sam]
```

Li: For route leak test add these commands (we use FRR):
```bash
# on transit router
show ip bgp neighbors 10.8.0.1 received-routes
show ip route vrf infra 10.0.0.0/16
```

Jordan: Observability: please ensure node-exporter and gpu-exporter labels include region=az15-edge and pool=preprod-gpu. Also add a cost center tag: cost_center=research.

Sam: Adding Prometheus scrape example to runbook: 
```yaml
- job_name: 'node-exporter-az15'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['10.10.3.2:9100', '10.10.3.3:9100']
      labels:
        region: 'az15-edge'
        pool: 'preprod-gpu'
        cost_center: 'research'
```

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for infra/az15 (staging) — no changes after Sam's last push.

Maya: OK. Proposed next steps: 1) patch runbook to use NAT Gateway as default for initial run to avoid quota blocking, 2) raise public IP quota in parallel, 3) NetEng to run MTU + BGP hold timer test in a blue/green dry-run on a small set. If NetEng OK, schedule full provisioning next Wed.

Priya: I can own automated checks (MTU, labels order, kubelet-ready gating). I'll open a PR with scripts.

Jordan: Capacity: @Jordan please request GPU quota for both 40GB & 80GB SKUs and ask about spot capacity floor. Put ticket link in runbook.

Jordan: on it — will post ticket ID in the runbook once requested.

Sam: Great. I'll update the runbook now with the MTU tests, NAT suggestion, SKU mapping table placeholder, and handoff checklist. Leaving an action items section at bottom so whoever gets the handoff can tick off.

Maya: Thanks — once the PR is up, @maya and @priya will do a quick review and sign-off. :thumbsup:

Sam: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/5423 — contains runbook + preflight scripts + sample terraform var overrides.

deploy-bot: PR 5423 created by Sam (files: runbooks/az15-init/README.md, runbooks/az15-init/preflight.sh, infra/overrides/az15.tfvars)

Li: I'll schedule the MTU+BGP dry-run for Tue 09:00 UTC and post the results in this thread.

Sam: Nice. Moving this to 'handoff pending' — tagging Capacity/NetEng/Observability.

Jordan: Assigned action items: Capacity (quota) -> Jordan, NetEng (MTU+BGP) -> Li, Automation checks -> Priya, Runbook updates -> Sam.

Sam: thanks y'all. I'll follow up with a short summary before the Wed run.
